title: Hand and pitcher pumps: leathers, valves, priming and frost
summary: Keep a hand or pitcher pump working: prime it with clean water, find air leaks, change the cup and valve leathers (soaked first), deal with foot valves, and drain it so frost doesn't split it or tear the leathers. Most failures are a dry or worn leather or an air leak on the suction side. Watch your fingers: the handle can fly up when let go.

materials.item: Cup leather (plunger leather) to fit the pump
Valve (flapper) leather to fit the pump
Seal kit for a deep-well hand pump (maker's)
Clean water for priming and soaking
Unscented bleach to clean parts going back into the well

steps.text: Find out which pump you have: a pitcher pump has its cylinder at the top and sucks water up; a deep-well pump has a rod running down to a cylinder under the water (Flotec pitcher pump; Bison FAQ).

If it won't lift water, check in order: is it primed, is the pipe end still in water, is there an air leak on the suction side, is the water deeper than the pump can lift (Water Source pitcher pump; Boshart Model 19)?

Prime a pitcher pump: fill it with clean water (boiled and cooled, or disinfected, unless you can vouch for it) until it runs out of the spout, wait 5 to 10 minutes for the leather to swell, then pump with short strokes (Flotec pitcher pump; Boshart Model 19).
steps.warn: Never work it dry: that can damage the cup leather (Flotec pitcher pump). Never prime with pond, ditch or flood water: it goes down the pipe toward the well.

steps.text: Stop air leaks: tighten the base bolts and re-seal metal threaded joints with PTFE tape or compound, but don't use tape on PVC pipe (Water Source pitcher pump; Flotec pitcher pump). Even a small suction leak stops it priming.
To change the cup leather, loosen the cap screw, lift out the plunger, unscrew the leather holder, fit the new cup and put it back together (Flotec pitcher pump).
steps.warn: Keep fingers out from under the handle: it can fly up when released on the downstroke (Boshart Model 19).

steps.text: To change the valve leather, unbolt the body from the base, take the weight off the old flap, scrape the old leather off, bolt the weight to the new leather and set it centred over the hole (Water Source pitcher pump; Flotec pitcher pump).

Soak the new valve leather in clean water before the pump is used again (Water Source pitcher pump). The cup leather swells during priming, so prime again and wait the full time (step 3). If it still won't lift, let the plunger soak a few hours and try again (Water Source pitcher pump; Boshart Model 19).
Decide about a foot valve: it keeps the pump primed, but then the pump stays full and must be kept from freezing (Water Source pitcher pump; Boshart Model 19).
Before frost, leave a pitcher pump's handle all the way up so it drains, or take the pump off the well if it has a foot valve (Water Source pitcher pump; Boshart Model 19).
steps.warn: Don't pump a frozen pump: frozen leathers tear (Water Source pitcher pump). If you lift the pump off the well, cap the open casing and keep children back from it (Flotec pitcher pump).

steps.text: Thaw a frozen pump with hot water poured into the top, or take it indoors and soak it in hot water (Boshart Model 19). Pour slowly and keep your hands and feet clear: hot water scalds.
On a deep-well pump, stop a drip at the rod with a quarter turn of the packing nut; if it keeps leaking, fit a seal kit (Bison FAQ).
steps.warn: A frozen lift rod can be stuck to its seal: warm the gland nut, don't force the handle (Bison FAQ).

steps.text: Keep a deep-well pump's weep hole working: water level below it, and the bleeder opened or hose taken off after use so air can get in and the head can drain (water level: Bison FAQ; air and bleeder: Simple Pump install).
Work a deep-well pump for a few minutes every week or two to keep the seals soft (Simple Pump install).

Clean anything that goes back down the well (Simple Pump install). Then boil drinking water for a full minute at a rolling boil until the well has been disinfected and a bacteria test is clean (Manitoba well fact sheet; Manitoba boil water fact sheet).

notes:
## Two kinds of hand pump
- **Pitcher (suction) pump:** the cylinder and plunger sit at the top, and the stroke sucks water up a pipe from the well. A leather cup on the plunger seals against the cylinder, and a leather flap (the valve leather) at the base acts as the check valve (Flotec pitcher pump; Water Source pitcher pump). Air pressure does the lifting, so it reaches only about 6 to 7.6 m (20 to 25 ft) at sea level, less at altitude (Boshart Model 19; Water Source pitcher pump); see [Driving a sandpoint well](#guides/build_sandpoint_well) for the lift limits.
- **Deep-well pump:** the cylinder hangs below the water on a drop pipe, driven by a rod from the handle, so it pushes water up rather than sucking it. These are the pumps that fit beside a submersible: see [Water from a drilled well with no power](#guides/build_well_bucket).

## What wears out first

| Pump | Wears first | Sign |
|---|---|---|
| Pitcher pump | Cup leather, then the valve leather; both are the parts the makers sell for replacement (Flotec pitcher pump; Water Source pitcher pump) | Won't hold prime, weak or no lift |
| Deep-well hand pump | Cup seal on the lift rod and other wear parts in the pump head and cylinder (Bison FAQ). Simple Pump puts the first seal kit at 3 to 10 years (Simple Pump install) | Leak at the rod the packing nut won't stop |
| Rope pump | The rope; pistons last about twice as long (Practica rope pump) | Frayed rope, less water |

Not every pitcher pump has leathers: Merrill's heavy-duty one uses a rubber-like cup in place of leather (Merrill FAQ), and Bison's Model 1900 uses buna rubber cup seals and a check valve and calls itself self-priming (Bison FAQ).

## Won't pump?

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Handle moves freely, no water | Not primed, or the cup leather is dry and shrunk | Prime; let the plunger soak a few hours (Water Source pitcher pump) |
| Lifts a little then loses it | Air leak on the suction side: base bolts, a pipe joint, a crack | Tighten, re-seal; any suction leak stops priming (Water Source pitcher pump; Boshart Model 19) |
| Water drains back between uses | Valve leather torn or not centred over its hole | Open the base and check or replace it (Water Source pitcher pump) |
| Sucks air or nothing at all | Pipe end out of the water, or the water is too far down | Keep the pipe end at least 1.5 m (5 ft) under water (Boshart Model 19; Water Source pitcher pump) |
| Handle frozen solid | Ice in the cylinder | Thaw it; never force it (Water Source pitcher pump; Bison FAQ) |
| Deep-well pump needs many strokes | The check valves leak a little over time | Normal: a few extra strokes (Simple Pump install) |

## Priming
Fill the pump with water until it runs out of the spout, wait for the leather to swell against the cylinder wall (5 minutes for Flotec and Water Source, 7 to 10 for Boshart), then pump with short strokes until the pipe fills; it may take more than one try (Flotec pitcher pump; Water Source pitcher pump; Boshart Model 19). Prime with clean water (Boshart Model 19; Water Source pitcher pump), boiled and cooled or disinfected if you can't vouch for it; what you pour in runs down the pipe toward your supply, so never use pond, ditch or flood water. If a pitcher pump has sat unused a long time, pour water into the top to wet the cup leather before pumping (Merrill FAQ). Never work it dry: that can damage the cup leather (Flotec pitcher pump).

A deep-well pump doesn't need priming, but its cylinder must be under water: pumping air for any length of time can damage the seals (Simple Pump install).

## Leathers
A leather seals only when it is wet and swollen. Water Source says to soak the valve leather before the pump is used again, and if the pump won't lift, to let the plunger soak up water for a few hours (Water Source pitcher pump); Boshart also says to let the cup leather soak for a few hours if the pump won't lift (Boshart Model 19). For a new cup leather the makers' own step is the priming wait with the pump full: 5 minutes for Flotec and Water Source, 7 to 10 for Boshart. Use clean water for all of it, and if the pump has sat unused for a long time, wet the cup leather again before you pump (Merrill FAQ). When you change the valve leather, scrape the old leather off the base so the new one sits flat (Flotec pitcher pump).

## Foot valves
A foot valve at the bottom of the suction pipe keeps it full, so the pump stays primed (Water Source pitcher pump). Water Source suggests one when water is 2.4 m (8 ft) down or deeper and Boshart at 3 m (10 ft) or deeper, but a pump with a foot valve stays full of water and must be protected from freezing (Water Source pitcher pump; Boshart Model 19).

## Frost
- **Pitcher pump, no foot valve:** after use, leave the handle all the way up; that tips the check valve and the pump and pipe drain back into the well (Water Source pitcher pump; Boshart Model 19). You'll prime it each time.
- **Pitcher pump with a foot valve:** the pipe stays full, and frozen water in it stops the pump and can split the pipe (Boshart Model 19). Take the pump off the well in freezing weather and keep the water in the well below the frost (Water Source pitcher pump).
- **Frozen anyway:** the leathers freeze to the body and tear if you pump (Water Source pitcher pump). Pour hot water into the top and wait; if that fails, take the pump indoors to warm or soak it in hot water (Boshart Model 19).
- **Deep-well pump:** a weep hole drilled in the drop pipe below the frost line lets the pump head and pipe drain after use. Bison uses 3 mm (1/8 in) just below the frost line; Simple Pump's standard 1.6 mm (1/16 in) hole is about 1.2 m (4 ft) down, or deeper if you ask for a custom one (Simple Pump install), so check either against how deep frost goes where you live. It works only if the water level stays below the hole and air can get in at the top: open the check valve's bleeder or take the hose off after pumping (water level: Bison FAQ; air and bleeder: Simple Pump install). A frozen lift rod can be stuck to its seal: warm the gland nut by hand rather than forcing the handle (Bison FAQ).

## Deep-well pump care
- A drip at the rod: turn the packing gland nut a quarter turn clockwise, then a little more if needed. Too tight and the handle gets stiff (Bison FAQ). If it still leaks and pumps easily, the seals are worn out: fit the maker's seal kit (Bison FAQ).
- Work it for a few minutes every week or two, even when you don't need water: it keeps the seals soft and stops mineral deposits building up (Simple Pump install).
- Leave the handle resting in its normal upright position; Simple Pump says never to tie it in the down position (Simple Pump install).
- Simple Pump wants two people to install it, and rests the whole pipe string on a safety tool across the well cap while each length is added so nothing drops down the well (Simple Pump install); pulling it for new seals is the same job backwards. Each 9 ft (2.7 m) drop pipe kit weighs about 5 lb (2.3 kg), so 135 ft (41 m) of pipe is about 75 lb (34 kg) (Simple Pump install). Keep liquid sealant and pipe dope off the drop-pipe joints: Simple Pump says it can interfere with the piston, and it supplies Teflon tape (Simple Pump install).

## Old brass and lead
Health Canada says brass faucets and valves can contain some lead, and that water which has sat in plumbing for hours should be run for about a minute before you drink or cook with it (Health Canada lead in water). Treat brass parts in an old pump the same way. Running it only clears the water that sat against the metal: the lead stays in the part, and a lead-certified household filter is only a stopgap (Health Canada lead in water). See [Lead](#browse/hazards/lead).

## After the repair
Anything you lowered into the well or opened up can carry germs in. Simple Pump cleans pipe, rods and the cylinder in 1 part bleach to 20 parts water before they go down, and removes any leftover solution (Simple Pump install). Use plain unscented bleach, and never mix it with ammonia, acids or other cleaners: see [Chemicals](#guides/reference_chemicals).

Manitoba says to disinfect the well and test for bacteria before using the water again after any repair or replacement of a well pump, and to boil drinking water until a test shows it is safe (Manitoba well fact sheet). A full minute at a rolling boil is its boil time (Manitoba boil water fact sheet); with no lab, keep boiling or disinfecting what you drink. See [Shock-chlorinating a well](#guides/skill_shock_chlorinate_well) and [Testing water](#guides/test_water).

## When the pump is off the well
Lifting a pump off the casing leaves the well open. Keep children and visitors back from open well heads (Flotec pitcher pump), cap or cover the casing straight away so nothing drops in or runs in, and don't lean in or climb in: Manitoba says not to enter a well pit or breathe the gases that may fill it (Manitoba well fact sheet). See [Confined spaces](#browse/hazards/confined_space).

## A submersible in the same well
If the well also has an electric submersible pump, its wires run under the well cap. Switch the power off at the breaker and tape over it or lock it off before you open the cap, and make sure it stays off while you work. Simple Pump warns that this wiring is only for people with the training or experience to do it safely (Simple Pump install). See [Mains electricity](#browse/hazards/mains).
